reproducibility_gaps: The pinned README, requirements.txt, CI workflow and packaging metadata disagree on supported Python/TensorFlow generations, so no single compatibility matrix is authoritative across the snapshot.
requirements.txt declares TensorFlow/Keras and a broad scientific stack, while active setup.py and egg-info requirements omit TensorFlow/Keras and declare a narrower dependency set.
Only protobuf and TensorFlow are exactly pinned in requirements.txt; most direct dependencies remain unpinned and no complete transitive lock or immutable container environment is provided.
SciANN is a reusable framework rather than one fixed application; no canonical dataset, experiment configuration, seed, checkpoint or expected numeric result is defined at resource scope.
The pinned README states that the project is no longer maintained and warns that TensorFlow/Keras changes rapidly, leaving future compatibility outside the documented tested state.
Tests, examples, training, prediction and CPU/GPU execution were not run under the Stage-3 static-only boundary.
notes: R2 is assigned at reusable-framework scope because source, exact MIT license text, installation routes, public API, physics constraints, architecture surfaces, training/evaluation interfaces, tests and examples are statically recoverable.
R3 is withheld because the environment declarations conflict, most dependencies are not locked, and no single end-to-end application contract is selected.
The README Apache-2.0 badge remains an explicit documentation conflict but does not override the exact MIT license text.
